title: Greetings & Politeness
description: The polite-form baseline. Say these correctly and almost every other interaction starts on the right foot.

phrases.registerNotes: Polite. Used until roughly 10-11am. Shops and hotels use it well into the morning.
phrases.animeNote: Anime constantly uses おはよう on its own — that is the casual clip. Dropping ございます to a hotel clerk or stranger is noticeably too familiar.

phrases.registerNotes: Neutral-polite, safe with anyone from late morning to early evening. Not used with close family.
phrases.animeNote: Fine as-is — this one carries over from media unchanged.

phrases.registerNotes: From around dusk onward. Standard entering a restaurant or hotel at night.

phrases.english: Excuse me. / Sorry. / Thank you (for trouble taken).
phrases.registerNotes: The single most useful word on the trip. Gets attention, apologises, squeezes past people, and thanks someone for going out of their way.
phrases.animeNote: Anime leans on ごめん and わりぃ. In public, すみません is the default — ごめん to a stranger sounds childish.

phrases.japanese: ありがとうございます

furigana.b: ありがとうございます

phrases.registerNotes: Full polite form. Use the past form ありがとうございました for something already finished, e.g. leaving a shop.
phrases.animeNote: ありがとう alone, さんきゅー, and あざっす are all casual/slangy. Keep ございます attached in public.
phrases.audioHint: ありがとうございます

phrases.japanese: ありがとうございました

furigana.b: ありがとうございました

phrases.registerNotes: Past tense — the interaction is complete. This is what you say leaving the shop, taxi or restaurant.
phrases.audioHint: ありがとうございました

phrases.english: Please. / Yes please. / I'd like that.
phrases.registerNotes: Attach to a request, or use alone to accept an offer. 'Bag?' → お願いします.
phrases.animeNote: 頼む / たのむぜ is the dramatic-casual version. Never to staff.

phrases.registerNotes: Also functions as 'I'm listening' — Japanese speakers say it far more often than English speakers say 'yes'.

phrases.english: No, I'm fine / no thank you.
phrases.registerNotes: The polite decline. A bare いいえ can feel blunt; 大丈夫です softens it and is what you'll hear declining a bag or a receipt.
phrases.audioHint: いいえ、だいじょうぶです

phrases.english: It's fine. / I'm okay. / No thanks.
phrases.registerNotes: Extremely flexible — reassurance, acceptance, or a soft refusal depending on context and tone.
Only ever on a genuine first meeting. Usually paired straight after with よろしくお願いします.

phrases.japanese: よろしくお願いします
phrases.english: Pleased to meet you / I'm counting on you (set phrase).
phrases.registerNotes: No clean English equivalent. Closes an introduction, or a request you've just handed someone.
phrases.animeNote: よろしく alone is the casual clip heard in shows. Keep the full form.
phrases.audioHint: よろしくおねがいします

phrases.registerNotes: Polite acknowledgement that you've followed an instruction.
phrases.animeNote: わかった is casual; 了解 (ryōkai) sounds military/blunt from a tourist despite being everywhere in anime.

phrases.japanese: すみません、わかりません

furigana.b: すみません、わかりません

phrases.registerNotes: Leading with すみません keeps it soft. This is the single most valuable escape hatch you have.
phrases.audioHint: すみません、わかりません

phrases.japanese: 日本語が少しわかります
phrases.registerNotes: Sets expectations early and usually makes the other person slow down without you having to ask.
phrases.audioHint: にほんごがすこしわかります

phrases.japanese: もう一度お願いします
phrases.registerNotes: Polite way to ask for a repeat without saying you didn't understand.
phrases.audioHint: もういちどおねがいします

phrases.japanese: ゆっくりお願いします
phrases.registerNotes: More useful than asking for a repeat at the same speed. Works on its own.
phrases.audioHint: ゆっくりおねがいします

phrases.registerNotes: Ask it in Japanese — opening in English can read as presumptuous. Expect 少しだけ ('only a little') often.
phrases.audioHint: えいごがはなせますか

phrases.registerNotes: Physical politeness — entering a room, stepping past someone, ending a call. More formal than すみません.
Textbook-correct but used less than English 'you're welcome'. A small nod, or いいえ, is very common instead.

phrases.english: Thanks for your work / good job (set phrase).
phrases.registerNotes: Recognition only — you'll hear it constantly between colleagues and staff. As a tourist you rarely need to say it.

phrases.english: I'm here as a tourist / for sightseeing.
phrases.registerNotes: Answers the most common question you'll get, at immigration and in small talk alike.
Heavier than English 'goodbye' — it hints at a long parting. Leaving a shop, ありがとうございました or 失礼します is more natural.
phrases.animeNote: Dramatic partings in anime make this feel like the default farewell. In daily life it is used far less than you would expect.

phrases.registerNotes: For an actual mistake you made, not for getting attention. For bumping into someone, すみません is the reflex.
phrases.animeNote: ごめん / ごめんね are the casual clips heard constantly on screen — fine with friends, too light for a real apology to a stranger.
